extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys and agents), parties appearing before the PTAB
extracted.subtask_short: ptab appeals and aia trials practice
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and procedural standards for submitting and litigating matters before the PTAB, including POP designation, ex parte appeals (including fast-track), motions to amend practice in AIA trials, and the LEAP practitioner program. Covers filing requirements, substantive burdens, timelines, and guidance on hearings and briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and effect of POP (SOP2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation of a Precedential Opinion Panel (POP) to rehear matters of exceptional importance involving policy or procedure in pending trials and appeals, resulting in binding agency authority unless otherwise designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOP2 (revision 10) establishes POP formation and that POP decisions create binding Board precedent unless otherwise designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for designating precedential and informative decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for nomination, review, and designation of Board decisions, other than POP decisions, as precedential or informative; and procedure for de-designating precedential and informative decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOP2 sets forth two paths for special designation (POP review and designation) and the processes to nominate and designate decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical issues appropriate for POP review
rubrics_metrics.description: POP hears cases that involve constitutional questions; important questions regarding statutes, rules, regulations; important issues regarding precedential case law; issues of broad applicability to the Board; resolving conflicts between Board decisions; and promoting certainty and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use POP for questions of exceptional importance or broad applicability; conflicts between Board decisions are appropriate POP matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP default composition and substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Default POP composition: (1) Director of USPTO, (2) Commissioner for Patents, (3) PTAB Chief Judge. SOP2 sets forth order of substitutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand who will sit on POP and substitute order when making strategic decisions about requesting POP review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request POP review
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party to a proceeding (e.g., an applicant appealing an adverse examiner decision, a party in a PTAB trial proceeding), and also the Commissioner for Patents, PTAB Chief Judge, or any other member of the Board may request POP review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both private parties and Board leadership may initiate POP rehearing requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request POP review (form and filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an email requesting POP review to Precedential_Opinion_Panel_Request@uspto.gov accompanied by a request for rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email submission is mandatory; the request for POP review must accompany a rehearing request in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP request content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The email must “identify with particularity the reasons for recommending Precedential Opinion Panel review” and include at least one of the following statements: (1) Decision is contrary to binding precedent (SCOTUS, CAFC, PTAB); (2) Decision is contrary to a constitutional provision, statute, or regulation; (3) Case implicates a question of exceptional importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific and expressly assert at least one of the enumerated bases to satisfy the submission requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP grant/denial orders and what they must include
rubrics_metrics.description: If POP grants review, a POP grant order is issued; if POP denies review, a POP denial order is entered into the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POP grant order includes: issue to be resolved, schedule for review process (briefing due dates), additional and responsive briefing and page limits, amicus briefing and page limits, and oral hearing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP oral hearing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral hearing will be granted if requested by the parties and as determined by the POP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing Order includes date/location, information on demonstratives, order for hearing arguments; hearings are open to the public; POP may decline even if requested per its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP amicus request form timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Amicus requests regarding a pending POP request must be made within seven business days of entry of the Notification of Receipt of POP Request into the case docket or patent application file and must include case identifying information (name, affiliation, any client represented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form allows explanation of why POP request should or should not be granted; consult published POP page for the form (published Nov 19, 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB anonymous decision nomination form usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Form (published Sept 24, 2020) allows any member of the public to nominate any PTAB decision for precedential or informative designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide as much identifying information as possible, brief description of reasons, and optionally name and email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest (RPI) identification in appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal brief must include a statement identifying the real party in interest at the time the appeal brief is filed; a real party in interest may include the inventor and any individuals or entities that have ownership rights or an assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must update the real party in interest if it changes during the proceeding (see 37 C.F.R. § 41.8). Example format provided in slides.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPI/privity burden for time-bar (RPX guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: In RPX Corp. v. Applications in Internet Time, LLC, the Board determined the petitioner bears the burden to establish no RPI or privy was served with a complaint alleging infringement more than one year prior to the filing of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of RPI/privity is fact-dependent and requires a flexible, practical, equitable approach to who benefits from redress.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPI identification not jurisdictional when no time bar (SharkNinja)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board determined it need not address whether a party is an unnamed RPI when such a determination would not create a time bar or estoppel under 35 U.S.C. § 315; identification of all 'correct' RPIs under 35 U.S.C. § 312(a)(2) is not jurisdictional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lengthy RPI analyses if there is no time bar implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factors applied for follow-on petitions with joinder
rubrics_metrics.description: For follow-on petitions accompanied with motions for joinder, the Board applies the General Plastic factors and performs a holistic review of those factors when deciding whether to exercise discretion to institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facts under General Plastic can weigh in favor of exercising discretion to deny institution; present a holistic factual showing when arguing under General Plastic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of petitioner stipulations on institution discretion (Sotera)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner’s broad stipulation to not pursue 'any ground raised or that could have been reasonably raised' addresses concerns of duplicative efforts and potentially conflicting decisions and weighed strongly against exercising discretion to deny institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad stipulation may help overcome discretion-based denials by showing the IPR is a 'true alternative' to district court proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of district court stay on institution discretion (Snap)
rubrics_metrics.description: A district court’s stay of litigation pending denial of institution or a final written decision can allay concerns about inefficiency and duplication and weigh strongly against exercising discretion to deny inter partes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of a stay favors institution when arguing against discretionary denial based on efficiency concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief core parts
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal brief consists of six parts: (1) Summary of claimed subject matter, (2) Real party in interest, (3) Related appeals, interferences, and trials, (4) Argument, (5) Conclusion (optional), and (6) Claims appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PTAB word template and PDF instructions available on the PTAB website to structure the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each of the rejected independent claims; not required for pro se applicants but may help the Board understand the arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If included, should identify, for each claim element, supporting disclosure and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals/trials identification
rubrics_metrics.description: List any prior or pending cases before the Board or a court that are related to the current appeal; a related case is one based on a patent or application you own and that would affect or be affected by the current appeal (e.g., continuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide case numbers and dates if available, or state 'no related appeals' if none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument requirement in appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument section should explain why the examiner’s decision to reject the pending claims is improper and should be reversed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on legal and factual reasons demonstrating error in the examiner’s rejection and tie arguments to the claim elements and record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion and claims appendix requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusion should briefly explain requested relief (e.g., reverse the examiner’s rejection). The claims appendix must include all claims on appeal, should not indicate prior amendments or reference non-admitted amendments, and should start on a new page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the appendix is clean and comprehensive; do not annotate prior amendment history in the appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year ex parte appeal timeline objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Timelines for a diligent appellant and PTAB fast-track can lead to a final decision in one year or less from final action; typical stages and target months are provided to show how appeals may proceed more quickly if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expedited/fast-track options and diligence in filing to shorten pendency; not appropriate for all appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-Track Appeals Pilot Program purpose and pendency goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot program to get ex parte appeals decided in 6 months or less; appellant requests expedition by filing a petition and fee ($420) for regular pilot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency goal is PTAB decision within six months; initial pilot was one year and subject to extension; check PTAB website for updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-Track Appeals eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying application types: original utility, design, or plant nonprovisional applications. Status: pending ex parte appeal (Notice of Appeal filed and Docketing Notice issued). Not limited to new appeals (petitions may be submitted for any currently pending appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm application type and appeal status before filing petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-Track Appeals restrictions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of granted petitions limited to 125 per quarter (500 total); hearings permitted with caveats; not available for applications already treated as special under MPEP 708.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor petition limits and timeliness; pilot availability subject to capacity constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID-19 Fast-Track Appeals pilot differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar to Fast-Track Appeals Pilot but with no fee; technology limit: application must claim a product or process subject to an applicable FDA approval for COVID–19 use; no time limit for the pilot and 500 total granted petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certify the COVID-19 applicability when filing; eligibility narrower on technology but fee waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-Track petition content and fee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition under 37 C.F.R. § 41.3; online forms recommended but not required; must identify application and appeal number and certify that the ex parte appeal qualifies. Petition fee under 37 C.F.R. § 41.20(a) is $420 for regular pilot; no fee for COVID-19 pilot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the cited regulations; include necessary certifications (COVID-specific certification when applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-Track hearing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant with a fast-tracked ex parte appeal may request oral argument. PTAB will try to accommodate time/location preferences but may schedule in any available hearing room or by telephone. Appellant cannot reschedule hearings and remain in the pilot program; may opt out and reschedule; may request video/telephone or waive hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan scheduling carefully—rescheduling forfeits fast-track status; during COVID all hearings are telephonic.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTA Pilot Program options for Patent Owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Owner (PO) has two options: Option 1 — request preliminary guidance (PG) from the Board on its motion to amend (MTA); Option 2 — file a revised MTA after receiving petitioner’s opposition and/or after receiving Board’s PG. Option 1 is not a predicate for Option 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PO may choose neither, one, or both options as allowed; pilot applies to trials instituted on or after March 15, 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTA pilot scheduling at institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Scheduling order entered at institution sets due dates similar to prior practice; schedule changed only if/after PO files revised MTA. Parties can stipulate to move dates but must leave time for PG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small changes: 12 weeks for MTA and Opposition to MTA, six weeks for reply and sur-reply regarding MTA (rather than one month previously).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Guidance (PG) content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If PO requests PG, Board will provide PG within four weeks of due date for Opposition to MTA. PG is a preliminary, non-binding initial assessment of the MTA based on the record so far; typically short; focuses on limitations added in MTA; does not address patentability of original claims; does not provide dispositive conclusions; no rehearing from PG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PG to shape a responsive revised MTA or reply; PG cannot be reheard directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner choices after Opposition and/or PG
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on Opposition and/or PG, PO may file: (1) Reply to opposition and PG; (2) Revised MTA; or (3) Nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing a reply, scheduling remains unchanged; petitioner may file a sur-reply six weeks after PO reply; no new evidence except deposition transcripts of cross-examination of any reply witness; replies are limited in scope to responses to PG/PO reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised MTA content and responsiveness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A revised MTA may include one or more new proposed substitute claims, and may provide new arguments and/or evidence explaining why revised MTA meets statutory and regulatory requirements. It may retain some proposed substitute claims from the original MTA but must provide amendments, arguments, and/or evidence responsive to issues raised in PG or Opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised MTA triggers a revised schedule and briefing; final written decision addresses only substitute claims at issue in the revised MTA if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on new evidence in replies and post-PG briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: No new evidence is permitted other than deposition transcripts of cross-examination of any reply witness for PO replies; where no PG, no further briefing on MTA; where PG provided, petitioner may reply to PG three weeks after PO reply, PO may sur-reply three weeks thereafter, and no new evidence is allowed with either paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve new evidence for revised MTA stage if permitted; adhere strictly to the 'no new evidence' rule during limited reply stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTA burdens of persuasion (final rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: New subsection (d) to 37 C.F.R. § 42.121 and § 42.221 (effective Jan 20, 2021) assigns burdens: patent owner has the burden of showing that an MTA complies with statutory and regulatory requirements for such a motion; petitioner has the burden of showing the unpatentability of substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For MTAs filed on/after Jan 20, 2021, craft filings knowing the allocation of burdens; evidence and argument should address the party’s specific burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board discretion when granting/denying MTAs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may, in the interests of justice, exercise its discretion to grant or deny an MTA, but only for reasons supported by readily identifiable and persuasive evidence of record in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may make of record only readily identifiable, persuasive evidence from related USPTO proceedings or evidence a district court can judicially notice; parties will have an opportunity to respond when the Board exercises this discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may raise unadvanced grounds in rare circumstances (Hunting Titan)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may, in certain rare circumstances, raise a ground of unpatentability that a petitioner did not advance (or insufficiently developed) against substitute claims proposed in opposing a motion to amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include where petitioner has ceased participation or where evidence not raised is readily identifiable and so persuasive the Board should take it up; due process requires notice and an opportunity to respond (e.g., supplemental briefing or discussion at oral hearing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable statutory/regulatory authorities and precedent for MTAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Key authorities include 35 U.S.C. § 316(d) and § 326(d) (PO requirements for MTAs), 37 C.F.R. § 42.121 and § 42.221 (rules for MTAs), and precedential decisions such as Hunting Titan, Lectrosonics, and Amazon/Uniloc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and apply relevant statutes, regs, and precedents when framing MTA and responses; §316(d)/§326(d) do not prevent considering unpatentability under sections other than §§102/103 for proposed substitute claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice regarding reissue/reexamination practice during AIA proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Office provides a summary of current practice regarding reissue and reexamination during AIA proceedings and factors the Office considers when determining whether to stay or suspend a reissue or reexamination proceeding that involves a patent at issue in an AIA proceeding and when to lift such a stay/suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider these factors when advising clients about pursuing reissue or reexamination in parallel with an AIA trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEAP program objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal Experience and Advancement Program (LEAP) fosters development of newer practitioners through incentives for oral advocacy and practical training to develop a bench of talent, improve case quality, and increase diversity within the patent bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAP aims to give junior practitioners substantive opportunities and training to improve representation before PTAB and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEAP eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify a patent agent or attorney must have: (1) three (3) or fewer substantive oral arguments in any federal tribunal (including PTAB), and (2) seven (7) or fewer years of experience as a licensed attorney or registered patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Substantive’ means arguments directed to the merits (not ancillary issues). The 7-year period begins with first licensure/registration and is not tolled for practice in a different field/jurisdiction or for years away from practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to apply for LEAP participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply for a specific proceeding after a hearing date is established by emailing PTABHearings@uspto.gov at least five (5) business days before the hearing and submitting a Request and Verification Form (sample combined form available on LEAP page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the sample form on the PTAB LEAP webpage and meet the 5-business-day notice requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEAP oral argument participation rules and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: A party with a LEAP practitioner arguing at oral hearing typically receives 15 minutes of additional argument time. The LEAP practitioner must have a meaningful and substantive role but need not argue for a specific amount of time. More experienced counsel may assist and make limited clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extra time is allocated to accommodate splitting argument time and to encourage parties/clients to allow junior counsel substantive roles; track and document the LEAP practitioner’s substantive role.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEAP training opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB offers free LEAP training opportunities including oral advocacy skills, preparing for oral argument, AIA trials mock argument, appeals mock argument, and the 'perfect' argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTAB's LEAP Preparation resources on the PTAB website to prepare LEAP practitioners for hearings.
